name: Hindware Home Innovation Ltd
title: Hindware Home Innovation Ltd - 542905 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Hindware FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 27% to ₹233 crore on 9% margin, while Q4 revenue fell to ₹663 crore from ₹699 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue was ₹2,510 crore (flat vs ₹2,523 crore), with EBITDA up 27% to ₹233 crore and margin at 9% vs 7%. Q4 revenue fell 5% YoY to ₹663 crore, but EBITDA rose 23% to ₹63 crore and PBT before exceptional items was ₹15 crore vs ₹2 crore. Bathware grew 10% in FY26 with margins up 160 bps, while pipes revenue declined and posted a PBT loss, with a March resin-price spike cutting inventory and sales. Home Innovation (consumer appliances) is being rationalised, with management guiding to EBITDA-positive in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Bathware (sanitaryware and faucets)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹1,520 crore (+10%), EBITDA ₹157 crore, margin 10.3% (+160 bps). Q4 revenue +10% with tile supply shortfalls; management says tiles non-availability cost about 2-3% of growth in Q4.

segments.name: Pipes
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹673 crore with PBT loss of ₹29 crore; management described FY26 as challenging. Q4 PBT loss of ₹10 crore reflected March resin-driven supply shortfall; April reportedly grew about 50% YoY.

segments.name: Home Innovation (consumer appliances)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹317 crore with EBITDA of negative ₹12 crore; Q4 revenue ₹80 crore and EBITDA negative ₹7 crore. Loss-making categories such as air coolers (except e-commerce), ceiling and other fans, air purifiers, water purifiers and furniture fittings are being discontinued.

guidance_outlook: Bathware: FY27 growth of 15-20% (value), with margin expansion of 1-2% YoY in FY27 and another 1-2% in FY28; management says it will reach the teens margin within two years.
Pipes: volume growth of about 14-15% expected; management said margins may improve as resin stabilises around ₹80-85/kg, but gave no margin guidance. Second half of FY27 expected stronger than first.
Pipes margin: consolidated (console) margin expansion of 1.5-2% per year for at least the next 2 years, per Sandeep Sikka.

Home Innovation: expects EBITDA and PAT positive in Q1 FY27 and positive for full FY27; targets consumer appliances revenue of ₹100 crore per quarter in Q1-Q2 FY27 and EBITDA margin of 8-10% in FY27-FY28.
Debt: net debt ₹708 crore; about ₹145-150 crore repayment this year; substantial reduction of 30-40% in net debt over next two years, with accruals going to repayment.
Demerger: NCLT Kolkata order reserved on second motion; final order expected in about 2-3 months, then roughly 1-1.5 months for exchange listing.
capex_capacity: Pipes Roorkee plant became operational at end of January 2026; ramp-up on plan, with more meaningful contribution expected in H2 FY27. Expansion phase now complete; FY27 focus on utilisation.
Bathware FY26 utilisation: sanitaryware plants ~82%, faucet plant ~89%.
Management said small capex will continue for manufacturing efficiency and debottlenecking.
Hintastica JV (Home Innovation-related): goodwill of about ₹34-35 crore impaired in Q4; a factory was disposed of in December 2025.
demand_pricing: Bathware price hikes: sanitaryware +6% (1 Feb 2026) and +7% (mid-April); faucets +15% (mid-January, brass ~₹600 to ~₹800/kg) and +3% (1 May).
Bathware FY27: value growth expected marginally above volume growth due to premiumisation; sanitaryware growth in early teens, faucets 3-4 points higher.
Market size cited: sanitaryware ₹7,000-8,000 crore; faucets ₹13,000-14,000 crore. Management said it is in top 3 in both sanitaryware and faucets; top 5-6 players dominate.
Channel and mix: institutional ~25% of Bathware revenue; Tier 1 ~35%, Tier 2 ~35%, Tier 3 ~30% (as stated, numbers total above 100%). Weighted dealers grew at very high double digits.
Pipes: PVC resin rose from ~₹68/kg (January) to ~₹114/kg (March), then stabilised near ₹80-85. Pipes March sales were about 50% of March 2025; April grew about 50% YoY and May-to-date about 30%.
Home Innovation: Q4 shortfall of ₹8-10 crore from raw material issues in e-commerce coolers, cooktops and hobs; tile supply shortfall of about ₹10 crore in March and ₹4-5 crore in April-May combined.

qa_highlights.question: When will Home Innovation turn EBITDA and PAT positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Nirupam Sahay expects positive EBITDA in Q1 FY27 and positive full-year profitability, citing portfolio rationalisation, new launches and premiumisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 15-20% Bathware growth target intact despite price hikes and inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price hikes have not materially hit sales, April momentum is strong, and it is confident of 15-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the competitive position and market share in Bathware?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it grew 10% in FY26, above market, gaining share; it is in the top 3 in sanitaryware and faucets, with the top 5-6 players controlling the market.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Home Innovation INR100 crore quarterly target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 was hit by raw material shortages in e-commerce coolers, cooktops and hobs (₹8-10 crore impact); it still expects ₹100 crore per quarter in Q1-Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Sikka said net debt is ₹708 crore, with ₹145-150 crore repaid this year and a 30-40% reduction over two years, not a fully debt-free target.

qa_highlights.question: What are the quantified tile supply impacts?
qa_highlights.answer: Tile supply shortfall was about ₹10 crore in March and ₹4-5 crore for April-May; regular supplies expected by June.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility (PVC resin, brass, gas and fuel) and possible further price increases; management said current hikes are sufficient for now.
Supply disruptions: tile supplies from partners, and fuel shortages affecting manufacturing partners; full normalisation expected by June.
Pipes: resin prices stabilising at ₹80-85/kg is critical for ASP and margin recovery; management declined to guide on pipes margins.
Home Innovation: whether Q1 FY27 EBITDA-positive target is met after a Q4 EBITDA loss of ₹7 crore.
Demerger timing depends on NCLT final order, expected in 2-3 months.
Real estate demand for sub-₹1 crore homes (raised by an analyst) and discount intensity in the industry.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth and margins, with April described as strong across businesses. Cautious on macro, raw material and supply risks, and noticeably vague on pipes margin guidance, deferring to raw material prices.

we expect it in Q1 FY27 itself, and the full year will definitely be positive.
So we should get back to regular supplies from all our suppliers by June.
We are targeting the 8% to 10% EBITDA margin in the consumer appliances business within the next two financial years.
